title: Live timeline: make tapping a track obvious, easy to hit, and quiet while dragging
acceptance: The Live timeline reads as tappable and says what a tap does (jumps playback to that track) without instructions elsewhere.
Each track target is at least 44x44 pt on a 390-wide iPhone, or the strip offers another reliable way to pick a track, so a tap lands on the intended track first time.

While a finger is dragging the timeline, Live does not show the "Waiting for music" banner and its actions; it shows at most a quiet seeking state, and the banner appears only if playback still has not progressed after release.
The design follows ritmofit_design_system; the owner reviews the design before build.
nextAction: Propose two or three design options for the timeline strip (affordance, target size, tap feedback, drag state) for the owner to choose; then build the chosen one. Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: Owner's iPhone Safari run on production af800c8 (Worker d05bb48f, SPA assets/index-ChxMwIpX.js), 2026-11-03 about 13:28-13:58 MST, ?playback-timing=1, class [QA] Audit Experienced Cycle (24 Apple Music tracks); console read by the Air conductor through Safari Web Inspector, plus the owner's screen recordings. Owner, in the Air session: "We need to improve that ui/ux. It's not obvious that I can tap those numbers, or even if I tap them what exactly tapping them does. It needs to be more obvious in design." and "It took a couple of tries of the failure of the ui/ux design. Not easy at all." One attempt at track 5 landed on track 4 (#5, trackIndex 3). A drag fired about 17 starts (#15-#32) and showed "Waiting for music" with Continue without music, Manage music connection and Skip track while the finger was still moving; it recovered on release.
Current strip: tightly packed track numbers along the bottom of Live.
